q: Under no circumstances ___ the dragon's hoard.
explain: Under no circumstances → inversion: should you + verb. Example: Under no circumstances should you open it.

q: So fierce ___ that even the bravest knights fled.
explain: So + adjective fronted → inversion with be. Example: So bright was the light that we shut our eyes.

notes.did the dragon roar: Did roar doesn't follow an adjective.

q: ___ it not for your warning, I would be lost in these stacks forever.
explain: Were it not for = if it were not for (present). Example: Were it not for you, I'd be lost.

notes.Had: Had it not been for is the past version.
notes.Was: Was isn't used in this inversion.
notes.If: If needs 'were': If it were not for.

q: Much ___ I admire her work, I cannot endorse this book.
explain: Much as = although (very much). Example: Much as I'd love to, I can't.

q: Try ___ he might, he could not decipher the runes.
explain: Try as he might = however hard he tried. Example: Try as I might, I couldn't sleep.

q: The riddle, ___ answer had eluded scholars for centuries, was finally solved.
explain: Whose for possession. Example: a riddle whose answer is simple.

notes.of which: Of which needs 'the answer of which'.

q: Little did she suspect that the librarian ___ her all along.
explain: Past perfect continuous for a long action before a past moment. Example: He had been waiting all day.

q: It is imperative that the scroll ___ returned before dawn.
explain: Imperative that + subjunctive be. Example: It is imperative that she be told.

q: Not a single word ___ during the entire ceremony.
explain: Passive: was spoken (nobody spoke it). Example: Not a word was said.

notes.spoke: Spoke is active: a word can't speak.

q: The more obscure the text, ___ the scholars become.
explain: The + comparative, the + comparative. Example: The harder the puzzle, the happier I am.

q: No sooner had the clock struck midnight ___ the books began to whisper.
explain: No sooner had... than. Example: No sooner had I left than it rained.

q: Should the dragon ___, offer it a riddle.
explain: Should + subject + plain verb = if. Example: Should you see her, say hi.

q: She talks as though she ___ the library herself.
explain: As though + past simple for something unreal now. Example: He acts as though he were king.

q: Be that as it ___, the prophecy must be fulfilled.
explain: Be that as it may = even so (fixed phrase).

q: Only by reading between the lines ___ the poem's true meaning.
explain: Only by... → inversion: can one grasp. Example: Only by practising can you improve.

q: Scarcely ___ the final page when the candles went out.
explain: Scarcely had + subject + past participle ... when. Example: Scarcely had we begun when it rained.

notes.did he turn: Did turn isn't used with 'when' here.

q: Never before ___ such a breathtaking manuscript.
explain: Never before → inversion; past perfect for before then. Example: Never before had I seen snow.

q: Come what ___, the library will stay open.
explain: Come what may = whatever happens (fixed phrase).

q: It's not as though he ___ warned.
explain: It's not as though + past perfect = he WAS warned (so no excuse). Example: It's not as though I hadn't told you.

notes.wasn't being: Wasn't being is continuous and odd.

q: ___ though it was, the riddle had a simple answer.
explain: Adjective + though + it was = although it was... Example: Tired though she was, she kept going.

notes.Bafflingly: An adverb can't start this pattern.
notes.However baffling: However baffling needs 'it was' without though.

q: She would sooner ___ the post than compromise her principles.
explain: Would sooner + plain verb. Example: I'd sooner walk.

q: Were it ___ to emerge that the scroll was forged, the scandal would be immense.
explain: Were it ever to... = if it ever... (formal). Example: Were it ever to happen, we'd be ready.

q: So engrossed ___ in the book that she missed the last bell.
explain: So + adjective fronted → inversion: was she. Example: So tired was he that he slept at once.

notes.she had: Had doesn't go with engrossed here.
notes.did she: Did doesn't go with an adjective.

q: It is vital that no one ___ informed until the birthday surprise.
explain: Vital that + subjunctive be. Example: It's vital that he be ready.

q: Not that I ___, but wasn't the deadline yesterday?
explain: Not that I mind = I don't mind, but... (fixed). Example: Not that I mind, but you're late.

q: ___ the archivist not intervened, the letters would have been burnt.
explain: Had + subject + not + past participle = if... hadn't. Example: Had she not called, I'd have left.

notes.If: If needs 'had': If the archivist had not.

q: The dragon, far ___ being hostile, offered us tea.
explain: Far from + -ing = not at all. Example: Far from being angry, she laughed.

q: Little ___ the apprentice know that the book was enchanted.
explain: Little did + subject + plain verb. Example: Little did we know.

q: Only in the final chapter ___ the narrator's true identity revealed.
explain: Only in... → inversion; passive is revealed. Example: Only then is the secret told.

q: Such ___ the force of her argument that the whole class fell silent.
explain: Such + be + noun (inverted) + that. Example: Such was the noise that we left.

q: Nowhere ___ a stranger collection of maps than in the Starlight Library.
explain: Nowhere at the start → auxiliary + subject. Example: Nowhere else can you see such stars.

notes.you will find: After nowhere at the start we invert.
notes.you find: Present simple would need do: do you find.
notes.found you: Found you puts the main verb first, which isn't inversion.

q: Only if the apprentice reads the rune aloud ___.
explain: Only if + clause first → inversion in the main clause. Example: Only if you ask will he help.

notes.the door will open: After only if, the main clause is inverted.
notes.the door opens: We need inversion: will the door open.
notes.opens the door: The main verb can't come before the subject here.

q: Not until the final chapter ___ who had stolen the moonstone.
explain: Not until + phrase first → inversion in the main clause. Example: Not until midnight did they stop.

notes.it is revealed: After not until we invert: is it.
notes.it reveals: It reveals would be active; the secret is revealed.
notes.reveals it: The main verb can't come first.

q: In no way ___ responsible for the dragon's bad temper.
explain: In no way (= not at all) + inversion. Example: In no way is this fair.

notes.we are: After in no way we invert.
notes.we're not: In no way is already negative, so no not.

q: Gone ___ the days when every book was copied by hand.
explain: Fronted adjective/participle + be + subject (literary). Example: Gone are the days of dial-up internet.

notes.have: Have gone would need a participle after have, and the word order differs.
notes.were being: Were being isn't used in this fixed pattern.

q: Into the cave ___, holding a single lantern.
explain: Fronted place phrase + verb + noun subject (literary). Example: Down came the rain.

notes.creeping the apprentice: Creeping is not a full verb, so the sentence has no main verb.
notes.did creep the apprentice: Did is not used with this kind of inversion.

q: Here ___ the moment we've all been waiting for!
explain: Here/There + verb + noun subject. Example: Here comes the bus!

notes.come: The subject is singular: the moment comes.
notes.is coming it: Is coming it adds an extra pronoun.
notes.it comes: It comes would need 'Here it comes', with a pronoun only.

q: Strange ___ may seem, the oldest book in the library is blank.
explain: Adjective + as/though + subject + verb = although it is… Example: Tired as she was, she kept going.

notes.although it: Although can't follow the adjective like this.
notes.as if it: As if means 'in a way that suggests'.

q: Try ___ they might, the robots could not climb the spiral stairs.
explain: Try as + subject + might = however hard they tried. Example: Try as I might, I couldn't sleep.

notes.though: Though isn't used in this fixed phrase.
notes.so: So isn't used in this fixed phrase.
notes.if: If isn't used in this fixed phrase.

q: ___ he to reveal the secret, the whole guild would turn against him.
explain: Were + subject + to-infinitive = If he were to (formal). Example: Were she to resign, we'd be lost.

notes.Was: Was isn't used in formal inversion.
notes.Should: Should + subject is followed by the base form, not to.
notes.Had: Had + subject needs a past participle.

q: ___ it not been for the owl's warning, the scrolls would have burned.
explain: Had it not been for = without (past). Example: Had it not been for you, I'd have failed.

notes.Were: Were it not for is present: Were it not for you, I'd fail.
notes.If: If would need had: If it had not been for.
notes.Should: Should it not been isn't a form.

q: Such ___ the dragon's hunger that it ate the entire feast.
explain: Such + be + noun + that (emphatic). Example: Such was his talent that…

q: ___ it a comet or a satellite, it was the brightest thing in the sky.
explain: Be it X or Y = whether it is X or Y (formal subjunctive). Example: Be it rain or shine, we'll play.

q: Far ___ it from me to criticise, but your spell is upside down.
explain: Far be it from me to… = I don't want to…, but (fixed subjunctive). Example: Far be it from me to complain.

notes.is: Is isn't used in this fixed phrase.
notes.being: Being isn't used in this fixed phrase.
notes.was: Was isn't used in this fixed phrase.

q: Long ___ the queen of the fairy kingdom!
explain: Subjunctive wish formula: Long live… Example: Long live the king!

q: If need ___, we'll sleep in the library overnight.
explain: If need be = if necessary (fixed subjunctive). Example: I'll go alone if need be.

notes.is: Is isn't used in this fixed phrase.

q: The council of owls demanded that the thief ___ the stolen feather at once.
explain: Mandative subjunctive: demand/insist that + base verb. Example: They insisted he leave.

notes.would return: Would return isn't the subjunctive form.

q: Would that I ___ able to read ancient Draconic!
explain: Would that + past (were) = I wish (literary). Example: Would that it were true!

notes.would be: Would be doesn't follow would that.
notes.be: Be is the mandative subjunctive, not used here.

q: She spoke quietly lest the sleeping giant ___.
explain: Lest + (should) + base verb = so that … not. Example: He hid lest he be seen.

notes.wakes: No -s after lest in the subjunctive.
notes.would wake up to: Would wake up to adds extra words that don't fit.

q: It's not as if the robot ___ us; it simply didn't hear.
explain: It's not as if + past/past perfect = an unreal comparison. Example: It's not as if I had a choice.

notes.has ignored: Has ignored is real present perfect.
notes.ignores: Ignores is a real present fact.
notes.would ignore: Would ignore doesn't follow as if here.

q: Suffice it ___ that the experiment did not go to plan.
explain: Suffice it to say = I'll just say (fixed phrase). Example: Suffice it to say, we were late.

q: 'Will the dragon come back?' 'I hope ___.'
explain: So replaces a whole clause after hope, think, expect. Example: 'Is it ready?' 'I think so.'

notes.it: It doesn't replace a clause here.
notes.that: That doesn't follow hope in short answers.

q: 'Is the library closed today?' 'I'm afraid ___.'
explain: I'm afraid so / not = a polite yes/no. Example: 'Is it raining?' 'I'm afraid so.'

notes.yes: Yes isn't used after I'm afraid.
notes.it: It isn't used in this short answer.

q: Mira can juggle five balls, and ___ her twin brother.
explain: So + auxiliary + subject = too (matching the auxiliary). Example: I can swim and so can she.

notes.so does: The first verb uses can, so the auxiliary is can, not does.
notes.can so: Can so isn't the right order.

q: The apprentice didn't notice the trapdoor, and ___.
explain: Nor/Neither + auxiliary + subject after a negative. Example: I didn't go, nor did she.

notes.the wizard didn't too: Too isn't used with negatives: we say either.
notes.neither the wizard did: After neither we invert: neither did the wizard.

q: You may borrow the telescope if you'd like ___.
explain: Ellipsis: keep to after like, want, need. Example: Come with us if you want to.

notes.it: It isn't needed after like here.

q: The spell wasn't so much difficult ___ long.
explain: Not so much X as Y = it's more Y than X. Example: He's not so much shy as cautious.

notes.than: Than doesn't follow so much in this pattern.

q: He didn't ___ say goodbye before he flew off on his broomstick.
explain: Not so much as = not even. Example: She didn't so much as look at me.

notes.as much as: As much as would mean equally.

q: The baby dragon can't fly, ___ breathe fire.
explain: Let alone = and certainly not (after a negative). Example: I can't walk, let alone run.

notes.never mind to: Never mind is used without to.

q: For ___ his cleverness, the inventor couldn't tie his own shoelaces.
explain: For all + noun = despite. Example: For all its faults, I love this city.

notes.every: Every doesn't fit this fixed phrase.

q: What ___ the storm and the power cut, we never finished the film.
explain: What with + nouns = because of (several things). Example: What with work and school, I'm exhausted.

q: The older the scroll, ___ it is to read.
explain: The + comparative …, the + comparative. Example: The higher you climb, the colder it gets.

notes.more hard: Hard takes -er, and we need the.

q: She is no ___ a magician than I am a mermaid!
explain: No more X than Y = just as untrue as. Example: He's no more a doctor than I am.

notes.less: No less means equally true, the opposite.

q: The map was every ___ as old as the legend claimed.
explain: Every bit as + adjective = just as. Example: She's every bit as clever as her sister.

notes.way: Every way isn't used before as.

q: The professor, ___ is often the case, forgot his glasses.
explain: As is often the case = as usual (as refers to the whole clause). Example: As is often the case, he was late.

notes.which: Which needs a noun or clause before it, not after the comma here.
notes.like: Like isn't used in this fixed phrase.

q: She explained, ___ it were, how to fold a star from moonlight.
explain: As it were = in a way, so to speak. Example: He's the heart, as it were, of the team.

notes.though: Though it were isn't the fixed phrase.
notes.like: Like it were isn't the fixed phrase.

q: By the time the eclipse ends, the astronomers ___ for twelve hours straight.
explain: Future perfect continuous: duration up to a future point. Example: By noon, we'll have been walking for six hours.

notes.will observe: Will observe doesn't show duration up to then.
notes.will be observing: Will be observing is in progress, without the duration up to that point.
notes.have been observing: Have been observing ends now, not at a future point.

q: I ___ you'd lend me your spellbook for the weekend.
explain: Past continuous for a tentative, polite request. Example: I was wondering if you could help.

notes.hope to: Hope to needs a verb: hope to borrow.
notes.have hoped: Have hoped sounds as if the hope has ended.
notes.had hope: Had hope isn't a verb form.

q: The castle was ___ to be demolished when the dragon moved in.
explain: Be about to + verb = very soon (here in the past). Example: I was about to call you.

notes.due for: Due for is followed by a noun.
notes.close: Close is followed by to + noun or -ing, not an infinitive.

q: No one ___ the professor's warning until the stairs began to vanish.
explain: Past perfect for an earlier action before a past event. Example: Nobody had noticed until it was too late.

notes.was heeded: Was heeded is passive and needs a different subject.

q: The apprentice ___ have been practising; her spells are flawless.
explain: Must have been + -ing = a confident deduction about a past activity. Example: You must have been waiting ages.

notes.can't: Can't have means you're sure it didn't happen.
notes.needn't: Needn't have means it wasn't necessary.
notes.should: Should have means it was expected but didn't happen.

q: Had I but known the stairs moved, I ___ them.
explain: Had I but known = if only I had known (literary third conditional). Example: Had I but known, I'd have stayed.

notes.had avoided: Had avoided belongs in the if-clause.
notes.avoided: Avoided is a real past fact.

q: The likelihood of the comet ___ Earth is extremely small.
explain: Noun + of + subject + -ing. Example: the chance of it raining.

notes.hits: Hits needs a subject and that.
notes.will hit: Will hit needs that: that it will hit.

q: Her ___ to share the prize won everyone's respect.
explain: Adjective → noun with -ness. Example: kind → kindness.

q: It was ___ of you to save me a seat!
explain: It's + adjective + of + person + to = describing behaviour. Example: It was kind of you to help.

notes.thought: Thought is a noun or past verb.

q: The dragon is ___ to wake before spring.
explain: Be (un)likely + to-infinitive. Example: She's likely to win.

notes.improbable: Improbable isn't used with to-infinitive like this.
notes.doubtful: Doubtful is followed by that or whether.

q: Brave ___ she was, the apprentice trembled before the sphinx.
explain: Adjective + though + subject + be = although she was brave. Example: Small though it is, it's powerful.

notes.however: However would need to come first: however brave.

q: ___ brave the knight, he would not face the sphinx's riddles alone.
explain: However + adjective (+ be omitted) = no matter how. Example: However hard the test, we'll pass.

notes.Whichever: Whichever is a choice between options.

q: ___ opens the box will be granted one wish.
explain: Whoever = any person who. Example: Whoever finishes first wins.

notes.Anyone: Anyone would need who: anyone who opens.
notes.Who: Who alone can't be the subject like this in modern English.

q: Take ___ path you like; they all lead to the castle.
explain: Whichever + noun = any one of a group. Example: Choose whichever colour you like.

notes.however: However is for manner or degree.

q: Not a ___ star could be seen through the thick clouds.
explain: Not a single + noun = none at all (emphatic). Example: Not a single person came.

q: ___ the apprentices passed the test; even the youngest.
explain: All of + the + plural noun. Example: All of the books are new.

notes.Every of: Every can't be followed by of.
notes.Each: Each needs of the: each of the apprentices.
notes.Whole: Whole needs the before it and a singular noun.

q: There's ___ little hope of finding the lost spellbook.
explain: Precious little/few = very little. Example: There's precious little time.

q: The two moons are ___ the same size.
explain: Much the same = almost the same. Example: The towns are much the same.

q: The wizard would rather the apprentices ___ the potions unsupervised.
explain: Would rather + person + past simple. Example: I'd rather you didn't smoke.

notes.don't mix: Present tense doesn't follow would rather + person.

q: She was overheard ___ that the treasure was buried under the oak.
explain: Passive of hear/see + to-infinitive (or -ing). Example: He was heard to shout.

q: I resent ___ called a 'little helper' by the older students.
explain: Resent + -ing (passive: being + p.p.). Example: I resent being ignored.

q: The inventor is reputed ___ over a hundred gadgets.
explain: Be reputed/said to have + p.p. = it is said that he did. Example: She is reputed to have met the king.

notes.to design: To design is about now or general habits.
notes.designed: Designed alone doesn't follow is reputed.

q: We were left ___ how the magician had escaped.
explain: Be left + -ing = continue to feel or do. Example: We were left speechless / wondering.

notes.to wonder at: To wonder at means to admire.

q: There's no ___ what the dragon might do next.
explain: There's no + -ing = it's impossible to. Example: There's no knowing how long it'll take.

notes.to tell of: To tell of isn't the pattern.

q: It was the potion, ___ than the spell, that turned him into a frog.
explain: X rather than Y = X and not Y. Example: It was luck rather than skill.

notes.more: More than would say it was more of the potion than the spell.

q: No sooner ___ than the lights went out.
explain: No sooner + had + subject + p.p. + than. Example: No sooner had we sat down than it rained.

notes.did the wizard speak: Did with no sooner is rare; the pattern uses had.
notes.spoke the wizard: Spoke the wizard isn't the pattern.

q: The scroll, the ink ___ had faded, was almost unreadable.
explain: Noun + of which (formal possessive for things). Example: a house, the roof of which leaks.

notes.which: Which alone doesn't show possession here.

q: There were two doors, ___ led to the dragon's lair.
explain: Quantifier + of which in non-defining clauses. Example: two answers, neither of which was right.

notes.neither of them: Neither of them would make a run-on sentence.
notes.none of which: None is for more than two.

q: The apprentice, ___ talent nobody had noticed, solved the riddle first.
explain: Whose = of whom/which (possession). Example: the girl whose bag was lost.

notes.of whom: Of whom would need different word order: the talent of whom.

q: It is high time the library ___ its ancient lift.
explain: It's high time + past simple = it should happen now. Example: It's high time we left.

notes.replaces: Present simple doesn't follow it's high time + subject.
notes.replace: The base form isn't used here.
notes.had replaced: Past perfect isn't used after it's high time.

q: I'd as soon ___ in the library as go to the party.
explain: Would as soon + base verb = would equally prefer. Example: I'd as soon walk.

notes.to stay: No to after would as soon.

q: Given ___ chance, the parrot would recite the entire alphabet.
explain: Given half a chance = if they had even a small opportunity. Example: Given half a chance, he'd sleep all day.

notes.a half: A half chance isn't the fixed phrase.
notes.the half: The half chance isn't the fixed phrase.

q: Little ___ the apprentice care that her robes were muddy.
explain: Little + did + subject + base verb = not at all. Example: Little did he care.

notes.has: Has would need cared and is present.

q: Only by working together ___ the giant puzzle.
explain: Only by + -ing first → inversion. Example: Only by practising can you improve.

notes.they solved: Past simple would need did they solve.
notes.solved they: The main verb can't come before the subject here.

q: So ___ was the music that even the stone statues seemed to listen.
explain: So + adjective + be + subject (inversion). The -ing adjective describes the cause. Example: So boring was the talk that…

notes.enchanted: Enchanted describes how someone felt, not the music.

q: The spell must be performed exactly as written, ___ it will backfire.
explain: Otherwise = if not (after a clause). Example: Hurry, otherwise we'll be late.

notes.unless: Unless would need a different clause: unless it is performed…
notes.lest: Lest means 'so that … not', which doesn't fit 'it will backfire'.

q: ___ the dragon spoke, the room fell silent.
explain: The moment/minute (that) = as soon as. Example: The moment I saw her, I knew.

notes.Meanwhile: Meanwhile is an adverb, not a conjunction.
notes.By the time that: By the time that suggests something finished earlier.

q: I'd have helped you, ___ you asked me.
explain: Inverted third conditional in the second clause: had + subject + p.p. Example: I'd have come, had I known.

notes.did: Did you ask isn't a conditional form.
notes.if: If would need had: if you had asked.

q: Not that it ___, but the dragon prefers its tea with honey.
explain: Not that + clause = I'm not saying it's important. Example: Not that I care, but…

notes.is mattering: Matter isn't used in the continuous here.

q: Build the sentence.
answer: Under no circumstances should the dragon be woken.
explain: Under no circumstances + should + subject.

q: Build the sentence.
answer: Try as he might, he could not open the door.
explain: Try as he might = however hard he tried.

q: Build the sentence.
answer: So vast was the library that we got lost.
explain: So + adjective + was + subject + that.

q: Build the sentence.
answer: Be that as it may, the quest must go on.
explain: Be that as it may = even so.

q: Build the sentence.
answer: Not a single page had the apprentice skipped.
explain: Negative object + inversion.

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: Scarcely had… when (No sooner had… than).

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: No double negatives: couldn't hear anything.

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: The + comparative…, the + comparative: the more…, the more…

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: Far from + -ing = not at all.

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: imperative that + subjunctive be.

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: Fixed phrase: come what may.

q: Fill the gaps with the words.
text: ___ though it was, the riddle had a ___ simple answer.
explain: Adjective + though + it was; adverb before an adjective.

q: Fill the gaps with the words.
text: Only by reading ___ the lines ___ one grasp the poem.
explain: read between the lines; Only by… can one…

q: Fill the gaps with the words.
text: Not that I ___, but the ___ was yesterday.
explain: Not that I mind (fixed); deadline = last day.

q: Fill the gaps with the words.
text: The dragon, far ___ hostile, served tea ___ any sign of anger.
explain: far from (not at all); without any sign.

q: Build the sentence.
answer: Never before had the village seen such snow.
explain: Never before + inversion: had the village seen.

q: Build the sentence.
answer: So tired was she that she fell asleep instantly.
explain: So + adjective + inversion … that.

q: Build the sentence.
answer: Were the river to flood, the bridge would close.
explain: Were … to + verb: a formal, unlikely condition.

q: Build the sentence.
answer: Little did they realise how famous she'd become.
explain: Little did … + plain verb: they didn't realise at all.

q: Build the sentence.
answer: Such was the noise that nobody heard the bell.
explain: Such was the + noun + that…

q: Build the sentence.
answer: All I want is five more minutes.
explain: All-cleft: All I want is…

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: Last night is the past: So loud was the music that we left.

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: Were … to + plain verb: Were he to ask.

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: After did use the plain verb: Not once did she complain.

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: The queue is one thing: Such was the queue that we gave up.

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: After should use the plain verb: On no account should you touch it.

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: by + -ing: Only by working together can we win.

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: Try as he might (past): he couldn't open it.

q: Fill the gaps with the words.
text: ___ was her talent ___ she won every prize.
explain: Such was + noun … that.

q: Fill the gaps with the words.
text: ___ the weather improve, the match ___ go ahead.
explain: Should the weather improve = If it improves; will go ahead.

q: Fill the gaps with the words.
text: At no point ___ the coach ___ giving up.
explain: At no point did + subject + plain verb: did the coach consider.

q: Fill the gaps with the words.
text: Strange ___ it may seem, the shy boy ___ the lead role.
explain: Adjective + as + clause = although; he landed (got) the lead.

q: Fill the gaps with the words.
text: Only when the lights went out ___ we notice ___ late it was.
explain: Only when … + inversion (did we notice); how late it was.

q: Fill the gaps with the words.
text: Hardly ___ the curtain risen ___ the audience gasped.
explain: Hardly had … when: the second thing happened at once.

q: Fill the gaps with the words.
text: Be it rain ___ shine, the festival ___ on.
explain: Be it A or B = whether it's A or B; the festival goes on.
